name: Pagu
catalog_quote: Stress in Pagu occurs on the penultimate syllable of the stem. Affixes and clitics are not stressed and their presence does not affect stress placement. In some dialects there is a tendency to add a copy vowel (a duplication of the vowel preceding the final consonant of the root) to many consonant-final roots. ... The addition of this vowel results in examples with stress which is not penultimate…

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim on Wimbish 1992:77 (page image read), with p.71 and p.78 supporting statements and Rule 1 confirmed in the scan we hold/scanned. (2) Deciding source is a dedicated 1992 phonology article with an explicit stress section; two later held works by the language's principal modern describer (Perangin Angin 2020, a paper devoted to Pagu stress placement; Perangin-Angin 2023 dictionary grammar sketch sec. 8) independently restate penultimate stress on the base/stem with affixes and clitics inert, so the fixed penultimate (stem-domain) coding is triangulated. (3) The one unheld work that outranks Wimbish in size, the 2018 HKU grammar, is by the same author as the held 2020/2023 statements; download failed again (an automated-access block), IA offline — listed as medium-priority list of works to obtain, not a risk to the classification. (4) The record's grade field is blank although the quote
